question: Test direction K0 -> Sumerian alongside common ancestry, borrowing and independent typology. K0 denotes the hypothesized earlier source continuing into Kazakh, not an attested ancient language identified by modern name alone.
hypotheses: H-KS: an earlier Kazakh-like source contributed to the formation of Sumerian
H-SK: Sumerian-related material contributed to later Kazakh ancestors
H-C: shared earlier ancestor without either attested language being the parent
H-T: independent similar typology plus chance comparisons
fixed_comparison_domains: Nominal plurality with animacy limits retained
corpus_rule: Use unchanged ETCSRI2026-10-24 snapshot; retain every unique Sumerian word node with N6=men/am/menden/menzen/mesh (accept actual stored spellings) and all visibly me-en forms. Export all matches and disagreements; editorial tags do not independently establish pronunciation or meaning.
follow_up_selection: For claimed men resemblance, obtain all numbered examples from Jagersma chapter29 sections identifying1SG/2SG forms; retain 2SG control and internal segmentation me+person. Identify physical references but do not assert photo validation if none inspected.
directionality_rule: Undated hypothetical K0 can be considered, but no geographic name or morphological similarity alone supplies its date or migration direction. A positive direction claim requires dated intermediates, regular correspondences and an asymmetric innovation or borrowing pattern.
older_steppe_reference: Seek primary scholarly description with cited inscription coordinates for early -DA/-DIn/-DAn forms; titles retaining conventional terminology are bibliographic names, not substitution of the author's preferred book vocabulary.
scope: One bounded source/comparison batch, no all-language claim, no book edits, no ancestry percentage, no invented probability of chance.
